headline: Canada's government has a new national council on AI, set up by Prime Minister Mark Carney to advise on strategy and on making the technology safer.
score_reason: Pool score kept: an official announcement on 2 Oct 2026 of an advisory body, but advice only and no new rules.
importance_line: Canada's government gets a standing group of advisers on AI benefits and risks, which affects Canadians and AI companies in time; it only advises, and the report does not say what power, money or start date it has.
summary: The CBC reports, citing a Friday news release from the Prime Minister's Office, that the council will bring together people from the public and private sectors to advise on speeding up AI use, building strong Canadian AI companies and AI infrastructure, making AI safer and protecting Canadian democracy. Named members include well-known AI researcher Yoshua Bengio, Mila chief executive Valerie Pisano, Senator Tom Pitfield and Patrick Pichette of Digital Transformation Canada.
notes: Background paragraphs in the CBC article about earlier AI incidents were not used because they could not be checked.
